Little Eddie Hoff, seven years old, is believed the superior of any child, male or female in all around athletics in New York City. While Eddie excels in many branches of sports, his latest triumph is in handling a rifle. He can box, now or shoot, both marbles and rifle with the best, but his fancy just now turns to the gun. "He was honored yesterday by Annie Oakley, famous markswoman and Cuba Crutchfield, noted roper in Central Park, where he demonstrated his ability with the gun and was shown how to twirl a rope. He surprised a large crowd by accomplishing shots, including the hit of an apple,150 feet away, and a visiting car held by Annie Oakley, at 35 feet. 13569—"We'll Show 'Em how to Fell Big Trees'—In the Great Oregon Forest, U. S. A.

Of the 94,560 square miles of land surface in Oreg' nearly one-third, or 28,843 square miles are covered with merchantable timber. The rich soil, the abundant rainfall, and the climate tempered by the warm Japanese current combine to produce forests scarcely surpassed on globe. Entire townships are reported having a stand of 100,000 feet per acre. Almos; the whole area between the coast range and the Cascade mountains, except the limited districts already cleared, is covered with forests.

The coast forests are heaviest and densest. Lane country, which extends from the ocean to the Cascade range, has more timber than any other county, but this is because of its size. An equal area in the northwest corner of the State, between the Willamette, the Columbia and the ocean, is much more heavily forested.

These small woodmen may live to be great lumber merchants, or to cultivate large farms where the forest now stands. At any rate, one would expect them to grow up with large and generous minds, and never to conduct themselves in a small or petty way. The tall straight trees should inspire all who see them to lofty thoughts and upright lives.

NO OCCASION TO GO TO GREAT EXPENSE IN DECORATING--PAPER TO
RARELY PLAY THE CHIEF PART IN THE ORNAMENTATION THIS YEAR.

The queer reveals of Hallow's are to be made more frolic- some this year by the introduction of new games and novelties in the favors and decorations. Here are some suggestions for the programme of the evening:

As erdeals by fire are peculiarly hallow's en sports an open fireplace, the kitchen cook stove or the cellar furnace, will serve as a centre for the various charms and ceremonies. First comes the spell of the nuts. Each participant, having been supplied with two nuts, names them and lays them side by side before the open fire. If these burn gently together, the augury bespeaks a happy wedded life, but if they "from each other wildle start and with a noise forever part" the prospect for marital happiness is dubious. Silly, isn't it, but Hallowwe'en comes but once a year.

Next pass around a bundle of twigs or splinters and let each guest light his or hers at the fire, repeating the old jingle Dingle, dingle, dowsy, the cat's in the well; the dogs awa to Berwick to buy a new bell.* If the brand continues burning emitting many sparks, there is money and good luck coming. If extinguished there is loss of property.

Beside all the time honored hallow's games, booking for apples, throwing apple pairings over the head to see the initial letter it makes, naming apple seeds and sticking them to the eye-lids to find out which sticks fastest one of the novelties to be introduced will be the candle jump. The way to do it is to light twelve candles, one for each month in the year and stand them in a row. Each guest jumps over the candles, taking every care not to extinguish one of them by the draft of the jump. That is if the desire is to remain a bachelor or old maid care should be taken. The extinguishing of one of the candles means that the extinguisher is to be married during the year and in the exact month that he or she called out when jumping over the candle.

For a contest with appropriate prizes threading wet pumpkin seeds on a string proves a slippery undertaking. A blind tandem race, in which a girl drives with red reins a blindfolded man through several rooms, returning to the starting point at the front door, makes much jollity. Three teams at a time should be started, the first one reaching the goal receiving the prize.

Here is another mirth provoking game for Hallowe's en: Seat the guests about a large table, provide each with a saucer of water in which fifteen letters of the alphabet have been placed upside down. The letters can be cut from an old magazine. Let each person blow the letters in his or her dish in a line, reverse them and spell the name of her future mate.

The decorations of the rooms can be done economically and yet with the most pictureque effect. For this purpose novelties in paper, some of which are illustrated on this page are being produced. They are inexpensive and look very well when tastefully arranged. There are paper napkins decorated with the symbols of the occasion, paper plates from which the grinning face peculiar to the evening will not disappear when refreshments are served en it, lamp shades and candle shades decorated withwitches' heads and

broomsticks and black cats with tails elevated at the proper earle angle,witches caps for favors and paper pie dishes, vegetables in immense variety and lanters to burn.

There is no need for an expensive outlay in flowers for this occasion. The decorations for the ancient festival can be secured from the corner grocery just as well, or the branches of autumn leaves and cabbages, the latter hollowed out and suspended from chandellers, make charming censers for holding candles stuck in bottles. Or the cabbages may be utilized as effective pieces for the table if filled with fruit. Pumpskins may be cut boat shape, then stored with fruit. Every one knows the decorative possibilities of pumpkins cut into Jack O' Lanterns, with the eyes of the Jack covered with red silk to give an eerie effect. Corn in sheaves or on the ear furnish delightful ornamentation for sseam rooms.

In the dining room ropes of cranberries, popcorn and scarlet peppers, sheaves of wheat, golden carrots, crimson beets, rosy cheeked apples and yellow pears form effective decorations. If the night is fine and mild a camp kettle might be suspended on the lawn and selected girls among the guests costumed in witches regalia to make a setting for the "brew", which might be coffee or anything that the hostess considers appropriate to the needs of her guests.

Of course the pumpkin has ever had the precedence in the matter of lanterns. But this year it has many vegetable confederates and turnips, carrots and cucumbers are all well established members of the clan. In the matter of candy boxes special ingenuity has been exerted. Does not, for instance, the presence of candy in the hollow handle of a broomstick restore all our lost belief in the potency of this implement? And does not the concealed hoard of bonbons in the steple hat of the witches set us to thinking that perhaps B. CETton Mather was right after all?

Hallowe'en supper should be served early as the hour before midnight must be reserved for ceremonies that can be tried at no other time. Any menu made up with nuts and apples in the ascendant will be appropriate. Of course there should be a dumb cake a fate cake or Hallowe'en cake.
